==English==
{{Commonscat}}

===Etymology===
Ultimately from {{der|en|orv|Москва|Москов-}}, originally referring to the {{w|Moskva River}}, probably from {{der|en|sla-pro|*mosky}}  (“swamp, dampness, moisture”). Perhaps related to {{cog|cs|moskva||raw bread}}, {{cog|sk|mozga||puddle}}, {{cog|pl|Mozgawa}}, and more distantly {{cog|lv|mazgāt||to wash, rinse}}, {{cog|sa|मज्जति|tr=májjati||to sink}}, {{cog|la|mergō||to dive}},<ref>{{R:ru:Vasmer|Москва}}</ref> all from {{der|en|ine-pro|*mesg-||to plunge, dip}}. Cognate with {{cog|ru|промозглый||dank}}. {{doublet|en|Moskva}}.

#* {{quote-book|en|year=1917| year_published= 9 September 2004 |page=71|title= The Darling and Other Stories|author= Anton Chekhov|tlr=Constance Garnett|publisher= w:Project Gutenberg|url= https://archive.org/stream/thedarlingandoth13416gut/13416.txt |isbn= 3734019680 |passage= The mother, Ekaterina Pavlovna, who at one time had been handsome, but now, asthmatic, depressed, vague, and over-feeble for her years, tried to entertain me with conversation about painting. Having heard from her daughter that I might come to Shelkovka, she had hurriedly recalled two or three of my landscapes which she had seen in exhibitions in '''Moscow''', and now asked what I meant to express by them.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=2005
|author=w:Bill Clinton
|title={{w|My Life (Clinton autobiography)|My Life}}
|url=https://archive.org/details/mylifepresidenti00clin/
|volume=II
|location=[[New York]]
|publisher=w:Vintage Books
|ISBN=1-4000-9673-1
|OCLC=60594427
|OL=8364562M
|page=49
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/mylifepresidenti00clin/page/n58/
|text=I was inclined to accept Yeltsin's invitation to go to Russia, but Tony Lake said '''Moscow''' shouldn't be my first foreign stop, and the rest of my team said it would divert attention from our domestic agenda.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Joshua Yaffa|title=Barbarians at the Gate|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/09/27/style/tmagazine/27moscoww.html|date=2009-09-25|passage=Everyone in '''Moscow''' uses the English term “face control,” though the phrase is often transliterated in print as “feis kontrol.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120203100707/http://travel.nytimes.com/2009/09/27/style/tmagazine/27moscoww.html?pagewanted=all}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Rhea Mogul|title=Russia can’t meet India arms deliveries due to Ukraine war, Indian Air Force says|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/03/24/india/india-russia-arms-delivery-ukraine-war-intl-hnk|date=2023-03-24|passage=An IAF representative told an Indian parliamentary committee that due to the Ukraine war a “major delivery” from '''Moscow''' “is not going to take place.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240615114942/https://www.cnn.com/2023/03/24/india/india-russia-arms-delivery-ukraine-war-intl-hnk/}}
# {{sid|en|Q1697}}{{place|en|oblast/and/federal subject|c/Russia|*surrounding the city, which itself is not part of the oblast|full={{w|Moscow Oblast}}}}.
#: {{alti|en|Moskva}}
# {{lb|en|metonymy|politics}} The [[government]] of [[Russia]] or the [[Soviet Union]].
#: {{syn|en|Kremlin}}
#* {{quote-journal
|en
|year=1927
|month=May
|author=w:Quincy Wright
|title=Bolshevist Influences in China
|url=https://archive.org/details/sim_current-history-forum_1927-05_26_2/
|journal=Current History
|volume=XXVI
|issue=2
|issn=0011-3530
|oclc=875826836
|page=302
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/sim_current-history-forum_1927-05_26_2/page/302/
|column=2
|text='''Moscow''' doubtless wants to make trouble for the Western Powers so far as she can without losing their recognition or encouraging actual hostility. She wants peace and trade and an opportunity for internal economic reconstruction above everything just now. It seems doubtful whether she expects to Bolshevize China, though she wants China fully independent of Western imperialism and friendly to her.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1956
|author=w:Harry S. Truman
|title=Memoirs of Harry S. Truman: Years of Trial And Hope
|url=https://archive.org/details/memoirsbyharryst012833mbp/
|volume=II
|publisher=w:Doubleday & Company
|OCLC=1036705143
|pages=345–346
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/memoirsbyharryst012833mbp/page/345/
|text=I could not agree with the tactics or approach of those who, like Chiang Kai-shek in a speech on July 3, 1950, wanted the U.N. to charge the Russians with the full responsibility for this Korean conflict and to demand that '''Moscow''' put an end to it. This kind of bluster is certain to lead into an impossible dilemma. If these suggestions had been followed and the Soviets had ignored the order, as in all likelihood they would have done, either the United Nations would have stood convicted of weakness or World War III would have been on.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1971
|author=w:Lyndon Johnson
|chapter=Thawing the Cold War
|title=w:The Vantage Point
|url=https://archive.org/details/vantagepointpers00john/
|publisher=w:Holt, Reinhart & Winston
|ISBN=0-03-084492-4
|LCCN=74-102146
|OCLC=1067880747
|pages=464–465
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/vantagepointpers00john/page/465/
|text=The translation of Khrushchev's letter reached me later that day, and I read it with care and with growing disappointment. It seemed designed for propaganda purposes rather than serious diplomacy. Khrushchev roundly denounced "colonizers" and "imperialism" as the major causes of past wars. Of course, he did not mention the Soviet Union's attack on Finland, the obliteration of the Baltic states, or the "colonization" of Eastern Europe by '''Moscow''' after World War II.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1987
|author=Shelomoh Naḳdimon
|title=First strike: the exclusive story of how Israel foiled Iraq's attempt to get the bomb
|chapter=
|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=8IhtAAAAMAAJ
|isbn=
|page=40
|passage='''Moscow''' said "Nyet!"}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1997
|author=Mervin Block
|title=Writing Broadcast News: Shorter, Sharper, Stronger
|chapter=
|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=MOykn3dMaJIC&pg=PA154
|isbn=1-56625-084-6
|page=154
|passage=Yet, a few US newscasters will go on the air at 6 pm or later and say, "'''Moscow''' said tonight.["] ... A careful writer would make his script read, "'''Moscow''' said today. ..."}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2009
|author=Svante E. Cornell; S. Frederick Star
|title=The Guns of August 2008: Russia's War in Georgia
|chapter=
|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=J4ta_TjGYBAC&pg=PA184
|isbn=978-0-7656-2507-6
|page=184
|passage=In addition, '''Moscow''' argued that Georgia had violated international law by introducing its forces into South Ossetia, a move '''Moscow''' said Tbilisi had committed itself not to do under the earlier CIS-sponsored peacekeeping arrangements.}}
